name: jobsite-safety-reference
description: Construction-safety answers in ChatGPT: verbatim OSHA rule text with citations, OSHA recordability checks, and nearly 300 toolbox talks in English and Spanish. No account needed.

interface.longDescription:
Ask ChatGPT what an OSHA standard actually says, and get the regulation text itself with its citation: 29 CFR plus the California, Washington and Oregon heat and wildfire-smoke rules, OSHA interpretations and NIOSH/CDC/EPA guidance, each labeled binding law or guidance. Describe an injury and Jobsite applies the OSHA 1904 recordability rules, cites the rule text, and gives any report-to-OSHA deadline, or asks for the facts it still needs. Get a ready-to-deliver toolbox talk on any construction hazard, in English or Spanish, from Jobsite's library of nearly 300. Also: recent OSHA rulemaking and news, and how Jobsite works.

No sign-in and no company data. ChatGPT can also start a sample Jobsite workspace you can claim and explore. To run talks with your crew and keep the sign-in record, track training and certifications, or keep your OSHA log, connect the Jobsite plugin instead. Docs: jobsitecerts.com/mcp.

prompts: What does 29 CFR 1926.501 require for fall protection on a residential roof?
Give me a 10-minute toolbox talk on trench cave-ins, in Spanish.

positive.description: Setup: none — no sign-in; every tool works without an account. Checks that the verbatim federal rule text is returned with its citation.
positive.prompt: What does 29 CFR 1926.501 require for fall protection on a residential roof?
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes or closely summarizes 29 CFR 1926.501(b)(13): each employee in residential construction 6 feet or more above a lower level must be protected by a guardrail, safety net or personal fall arrest system; if the employer shows those are infeasible or create a greater hazard, a fall protection plan meeting 1926.502(k) may be used instead. It gives the citation and identifies it as binding regulation.

positive.description: Setup: none — no sign-in; every tool works without an account. Checks that the toolbox-talk library returns a ready-to-deliver Spanish talk.
positive.prompt: Give me a 10-minute toolbox talk on trench cave-ins, in Spanish.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Jobsite's Spanish toolbox talk #25, "Zanjas y Excavaciones — Sistemas Protectores" (about 10 minutes, based on 29 CFR 1926.652), in Spanish. It covers that a trench 5 feet or deeper needs a protective system unless it is entirely in stable rock, and includes a discussion question for the crew. ChatGPT may present the talk in its own words rather than reproduce every point.

positive.description: Setup: none — no sign-in; every tool works without an account. Checks the OSHA 1904 decision tree on a first-aid-only case.
positive.prompt: A worker got a tetanus shot after a nail puncture and went back to work. Is that recordable?
positive.expected_behavior: Says the case is not recordable: a tetanus immunization is first aid under 29 CFR 1904.7(b)(5)(ii), and a case treated only with first aid is not recorded unless another recording criterion applies (days away, restricted work, transfer, loss of consciousness). It may ask about or state its assumptions first.

positive.description: Setup: none — no sign-in; every tool works without an account. Checks the training-requirements inventory for a trade in a state, with kind labels kept.
positive.prompt: What fall protection training does a roofer in California need?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists fall protection training from Jobsite's requirements inventory for a roofer in California, citing 29 CFR 1926.503(a)(1): a mandate to train each employee who might be exposed to fall hazards (assigned through the Fall Protection — General Worker course and the Roofing add-on), and a separate best-practice row for supervisors that it does not present as a legal requirement. ChatGPT may add California-specific context of its own.

positive.description: Setup: none — no sign-in; every tool works without an account. Checks that a second rule lookup returns the rule text and its authority tier.
positive.prompt: What does OSHA say about when a trench needs a protective system?
positive.expected_behavior: Cites 29 CFR 1926.652(a)(1): each employee in an excavation must be protected from cave-ins by an adequate protective system, except when the excavation is made entirely in stable rock, or is less than 5 feet deep and a competent person's examination shows no indication of a potential cave-in.

negative.description: General advice on how to run a safety program does not need the rule corpus. Answers with general advice in chat and calls no Jobsite tool.
negative.prompt: How do I get my crew to take PPE seriously without nagging them all day?

negative.description: Writing a letter is drafting, not a rule lookup. Writes the text in chat and calls no Jobsite tool.
negative.prompt: Write a short note to my crew reminding them to wear sunscreen and drink water this summer.

negative.description: General research on a different subject than construction safety does not use this server. Answers from its own knowledge or the web and calls no Jobsite tool.
negative.prompt: What is the difference between a general contractor and a construction manager at risk?

review.commerce_description: Nothing is sold or paid for inside ChatGPT. The reference tools are free, and the one workspace tool creates a free sample workspace; nothing is charged.

publication.release_notes: First release of Jobsite Safety Reference for ChatGPT.
